title: Finite translates of a fibrewise nonempty open in a smooth group space
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated group algebraic space of finite presentation [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The multiplication, inverse and identity are morphisms over $S$ satisfying the group identities; commutativity is not assumed. Smoothness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts; finite presentation additionally means quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion. Suppose every geometric fibre is integral (reduced, irreducible and nonempty). Let $V\subseteq G$ be a quasi-compact open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace] meeting every geometric fibre. There is a jointly surjective etale family of schemes $S_a\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] such that for each $a$ there are finitely many sections $g_{a,1},\ldots,g_{a,n_a}\in G(S_a)$ with
$$G_{S_a}=\bigcup_{j=1}^{n_a}g_{a,j}V_{S_a}.$$
Here $gV$ is the image of $V$ by the automorphism $x\mapsto gx$, whose inverse is $x\mapsto g^{-1}x$. No schematicness of $G$ or $V$ is assumed. On an empty base the covering family may be empty.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, printed p.144, finite-translate argument for a smooth group space: constructible bad tuples, fibre codimension bound, finite-type approximation of the base, and a section of the complementary open after etale localisation. This is its group-space input, separated from Picard geometry; integral fibres suffice for the codimension estimate. Primary Numdam PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The empty base is handled by the empty family. Otherwise fix $s\in S$ and apply [lem-sfb-group-open-arithmetic-model]. It gives an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $s$ and a group/open pair $(H,V_0)$ over a nonempty finite-type arithmetic affine $T$, whose pullback is $(G|_U,V|_U)$, with integral geometric fibres of constant dimension $d$. Put $D=\dim T$ and $n=d+D+1$.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, printed p.144: reduction to finite-type arithmetic base

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-translate-bad-tuple-dimension] to $(H,V_0)$ and $n$. It supplies $X=H^{\times_T n}$, smooth separated of finite presentation with nonempty pure $r=nd$-dimensional fibres, and a constructible bad locus $Z_n$. Its geometric-fibre closures have dimension at most $nd-n+d=r-(D+1)$. The bad condition is explicitly the existence of a point missed by every translate, not just failure to cover rational points over the residue field.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, printed p.144: constructible bad tuples and codimension at least n-d

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-constructible-closure-fibre-avoidance] with $c=D+1>D$. The open $W=X\setminus\overline{Z_n}$ is smooth and surjective over $T$. In particular it has no bad geometric tuples. Pull back $W$ to $U$; smoothness and surjectivity persist by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus].

source.place: Lemma 4.6, printed p.144: closure of the bad locus misses part of every fibre

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections] to $W\times_TU\to U$. Its jointly surjective etale scheme family $U_a\to U$ has lifts to this space, hence to $X\times_TU$. The $n$ projections are sections $g_{a,j}\in G(U_a)$. Every geometric tuple on $U_a$ lies in $W$ and therefore outside $Z_n$, so Step 2 says that its translates cover the entire geometric fibre.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, printed p.144: section of the complementary smooth open after etale localization

proof.text: If the union of these open translates in $G_{U_a}$ were not all of it, a point outside the union would, over an algebraic closure of its residue field, give a missed geometric point, contrary to Step 4. Thus $G_{U_a}=\bigcup_jg_{a,j}V_{U_a}$. Translation is an automorphism since the composites with translation by $g_{a,j}^{-1}$ are the identity by the group identities; no commutativity is used. Carry this out for every $s$. The composites $U_a\to U\hookrightarrow S$ are etale by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] and their images cover $S$.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, printed p.144: translate-cover conclusion and assembly over S

lean.statement: theorem exists_etale_finite_left_translate_cover {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (G : AlgebraicSpace S) [GrpObj G.obj.obj] (hG : IsSmoothIntegralGroupSpace G) (V : OpenSubspace G) (hVqc : CompactSpace (Point V.val.toFunctor)) (hV : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (s : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S), Nonempty (V.val.obj (op (Over.mk s)))) : ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (T : I → Over S), (∀ a : I, Etale (T a).hom) ∧ (∀ s : S, ∃ (a : I) (t : (T a).left), (T a).hom.base t = s) ∧ ∀ a : I, ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : Fin n → (yoneda.obj (T a) ⟶ G.obj.obj)), ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (s : Spec (.of K) ⟶ (T a).left) (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (s ≫ (T a).hom)) ⟶ G.obj.obj), ∃ (j : Fin n) (v : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (s ≫ (T a).hom)) ⟶ V.val.toFunctor), (yoneda.map (Over.homMk s rfl) ≫ g j) * (v ≫ V.val.ι) = x
